## New cells from old cells

**Cell division** is the process by which new cells are formed from pre-existing cells. It allows living things to grow, repair damaged tissues and reproduce. Skin cells, for example, divide continuously to replace cells that are lost regularly.

<!-- STEP -->
## Division goes on every day

Every day, an estimated hundreds of billions of cells in your body are replaced. That is almost 1 per cent of all the cells in your body.

<!-- STEP -->
## Two major types

Both prokaryotic and eukaryotic cells divide, but eukaryotic cells divide in a more controlled and orderly manner, by a process called the **cell cycle**. There are two major types of cell division:

- **Mitosis**, for normal growth, repair, maintenance and asexual reproduction.
- **Meiosis**, for sexual reproduction and creating genetic diversity.
